What Grade Do I Need on My Final to Pass?

Calculate the final exam score needed to pass or reach a target grade, with weighted examples and gradebook checks.

Final grade calculator ↗Weighted grade calculator ↗GPA calculator ↗
Worked final-exam examples, assuming the final is the only remaining assessment
Current gradeTargetFinal weightRequired final score
70%60%40%45%
82%85%30%92%
65%90%20%190%: target unreachable
90%60%20%−60%: target already met mathematically

Use three numbers from your course

You need your current average for completed work, the final exam’s percentage weight and your target course grade. This calculation assumes the final is the only ungraded component. If a project or another exam is still missing, combine the remaining work appropriately or use the weighted-grade calculator to model all components. Use the pass threshold from your syllabus rather than assuming one percentage works everywhere.

Check whether the displayed grade excludes missing work

A gradebook’s current average and its total after ungraded work is included can differ. In Canvas, the current-grade calculation can be limited to graded assignments, while the total includes graded and ungraded assignments. Inspect the setting and your course weights before copying a number. If unsure, ask your instructor which figure represents completed coursework excluding the final.

Rearrange the weighted-average formula

Overall grade = current × (1 − weight) + final × weight. Write weight as a decimal: a 30% final uses 0.30. Solving for the exam gives required final = [target − current × (1 − weight)] ÷ weight. Use percentages consistently for current, target and final. A final worth zero percent cannot change your grade and cannot be used as the divisor.

Worked example: the score needed to pass

Suppose completed work averages 70%, the final counts for 40%, and the course pass mark is 60%. Completed work contributes 70 × 0.60 = 42 percentage points. You need 60 − 42 = 18 more points from the final. Divide by its 0.40 weight: a 45% final gives 42 + 45 × 0.40 = 60% overall. This is a course-pass calculation, not a claim that 45% passes the exam itself.

Worked example: reaching a higher target

With a current average of 82%, a 30%-weighted final and an 85% target, completed work contributes 57.4 points. The final must add 27.6 points, so 27.6 ÷ 0.30 = 92% is required. A final score of 90% would give 84.4% overall. Use the calculator’s what-if table to compare realistic scores before planning how much improvement is needed.

Interpret results above 100% or below zero

A result above 100% means the target cannot be reached with an ordinary 0–100% final under these assumptions. For example, current 65%, target 90% and weight 20% require 190%. A result below zero means completed work already reaches the target mathematically. It does not excuse missing a compulsory exam or override a minimum final-exam mark.

Apply course rules before treating the result as final

Check minimum exam marks, attendance, dropped assessments, extra credit and rounding. A course may require a minimum exam score even when the weighted average passes. Keep full precision until the final step and follow the institution’s rounding rule. US, UK, Canadian and Australian institutions can use different scales; this percentage formula does not determine an official GPA, letter grade or degree classification.

Common questions

What do I need on my final to pass?

Use your course pass mark as the target. For a 70% current average, a 40%-weighted final and a 60% pass mark, completed work contributes 42 points. The exam must contribute 18 more, so 18 ÷ 0.40 = 45% is required. A separate minimum-exam rule can change the result.

My gradebook includes the final as zero. Which grade should I enter?

Enter the average for completed coursework, excluding the final. A total that counts the missing final as zero is a different number. Check your gradebook settings or calculate the completed-work average before using the calculator.

Can I round the required score down?

Rounding down can leave your overall grade below the target. Follow your course policy. If the calculated threshold is 86.67% and only whole percentages are possible, 87% reaches it; 86% does not under the same formula.
